title: Symmetry-Aware Residual Learning of Few-Body Molecular Wave Functions
abstract: arXiv:2611.33576v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Ultracold polar molecules are a highly controllable platform for engineering quantum matter, but modeling their few-body properties remains computationally challenging. Their anisotropic long-range interactions and rich internal structure lead to high-dimensional eigenvalue problems for which conventional grid-based solvers are largely restricted to two-molecule systems. To address this limitation, we introduce a physics-informed neural variational method that exploits known physical structure of the molecular wave function. Our key idea is to factor the wave function into analytic and neural components. The analytic component encodes rotational symmetry and asymptotic decay, while the neural residual learns the remaining intermediate-range behavior. translated_title: 对称性感知的少体分子波函数残差学习
translated_abstract: 超冷极性分子是工程化量子物质的高度可控平台，但对其少体性质的建模在计算上仍极具挑战性。其各向异性的长程相互作用和丰富的内部结构导致了高维本征值问题，而传统的基于网格的求解器在很大程度上仅限于处理双分子系统。为解决这一局限，我们引入了一种物理信息驱动的神经变分方法，该方法充分利用了分子波函数已知的物理结构。我们的核心思想是将波函数分解为解析分量和神经分量：解析分量编码旋转对称性和渐近衰减行为，而神经残差部分学习剩余的中程行为。这种分解在不依赖临时近似或针对特定问题的离散网格的情况下，有效降低了问题的有效维度。我们将我们的方法与高精度基准进行了比较验证。
tldr: 该论文提出一种物理信息神经变分方法，将分子波函数分解为编码旋转对称性与渐近衰减的解析分量和神经残差分量，从而在不依赖离散网格的情况下有效降低少体极性分子系统高维本征值问题的求解难度。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a physics-informed neural variational method that factors molecular wave functions into an analytic component (encoding rotational symmetry and asymptotic decay) and a neural residual, effectively reducing the dimensionality of few-body molecular eigenvalue problems beyond the reach of conventional grid-based solvers.
